references.purpose: Smithy operation and member definitions; requiresCompatibilities omission, essential-container defaults, dependency conditions

primarySources.finding: A launchType and capacityProviderStrategy are mutually exclusive. With neither provided, cluster defaultCapacityProviderStrategy is used. FARGATE launch type is on-demand; Fargate Spot requires capacity-provider strategy. No RunTask was called.
Same omitted-launchType/strategy contract: use cluster defaultCapacityProviderStrategy. No CreateService was called.
Current launchType section specifies default capacityProviderStrategy when launch type is omitted; not a blanket Fargate launch-type default.

Console selection differs from API omission: console chooses cluster default strategy, otherwise custom FARGATE strategy if Fargate providers exist, otherwise custom ASG strategy, otherwise Fargate launch type. Do not copy console defaults into API behavior.

After June 12 2025, removing capacity-provider strategy may fall back to cluster default or error when no launch type exists. Pre-change services have distinct EC2/FARGATE fallback cases. This is update behavior, not evidence of blanket API-create EC2 default.
CreateCluster attempts service-linked-role creation; named clusters avoid default cluster mutation. FARGATE and FARGATE_SPOT capacity providers can be associated without compute.
AWSServiceRoleForECS is shared and may be provider-created. Preflight verified an existing role from 2025; probe never modifies or deletes it.
Unqualified family selects latest ACTIVE revision. Documentation says INACTIVE describe only while referenced; retain live observations separately rather than normalizing to this statement.

Deregister before delete. Delete transitions INACTIVE to DELETE_IN_PROGRESS; family name/revision history can be retained and revision increments after recreation. DELETE_IN_PROGRESS is not verified absence.
FARGATE compatibility enforces supported CPU/memory combinations even when EC2 is also specified. Linux/Windows supported combinations differ; CPU/memory units may be normalized.

Timeout admission captured 2026-09-16 in account 000000000000, us-east-1, family stackd-ecs-timeouts-3b23bf6c56. Both explicit startTimeout and stopTimeout reject -1, 0, and 1 with ClientException for FARGATE and EC2; 2 is accepted. Omitted fields stay omitted. FARGATE startTimeout 120 and 121 are accepted despite the documented 2-120 range. FARGATE stopTimeout 120 is accepted and 121 rejected; EC2 and omitted compatibility accept stopTimeout 121 but exclude FARGATE from returned compatibilities. Mixed EC2/FARGATE enforces the stop cap. Explicit accepted timeouts add ecs.capability.container-ordering. Registration evidence only: no task execution or runtime-upper-bound claim. All 13 owned revisions were deregistered and deletion accepted, with no failures; ACTIVE/INACTIVE lists empty, all 13 still DELETE_IN_PROGRESS at final observation, not verified absent.

limits: No RunTask or CreateService; default launch behavior is documentation-grounded, not compute-probed.
No IAM role creation, log-group creation, compute, networking, public IP, account-setting mutation or paid infrastructure requested.
